A.depoimento: I am sending my forces to capture the nearby neutral villages of Santarem and Evora to expand my kingdom. I am also building more spearmen in my capital, Lisboa, to secure it and prepare for future campaigns.
A.plano: Capture the two visible neutral villages, Santarem and Evora, to expand my territory and increase resource production. Build 2 spearmen in Lisboa to maintain a garrison. March on both targets simultaneously with split forces.

B.depoimento: Built two spearmen in Barcelona and dispatched our knights to seize the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona, expanding our control.
B.plano: Captured Tarragona and Girona, now hold 3 villages. Next turn, reinforce new villages, build more troops (especially knights) to push toward enemy capital while maintaining defense.

A.depoimento: I ordered the armies of Santarem and Evora to strike the neutral villages of Coimbra and Faro, while Lisboa strengthens its garrison. The enemy remains unseen in the north.
A.plano: Capture Coimbra and Faro to expand territory and secure more resource production. Build 2 spearmen in Lisboa to maintain a garrison. Avoid attacking Badajoz this turn as it is better defended and leave it for later.

B.depoimento: Last turn we secured Tarragona and Girona. This turn we forged a new knight in Barcelona, dispatched our knights to seize Castellon and Zaragoza, and sent our archers on the road to Huesca. Our banner expands eastward.
B.plano: Next turn, reinforce Castellon and Zaragoza with incoming troops, continue building knights in Barcelona, and march archers to capture Huesca. Keep a defensive garrison in each owned village to prevent enemy counter‑attacks.

A.depoimento: Our armies march on Badajoz and Porto, seeking to claim these strategic crossings. In our forges, spearmen are being forged to swell our ranks. With each village we take, our kingdom grows stronger. We shall expand our territory and secure our borders.
A.plano: Capture Badajoz and Porto to expand territory and secure more resource production. Build spearman in Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to increase army size. Next turn, plan to attack Salamanca from Porto and Sevilha from Badajoz. Do not attack the enemy capital yet; focus on consolidating gains.

B.depoimento: Built one knight in Barcelona and two spearmen each in Tarragona and Girona. Sent three spearmen from Barcelona to Tarragona, two spearmen to Girona, and one knight to Castellon to strengthen our front lines.
B.plano: Next turn, reinforce Tarragona and Girona with incoming troops, continue building knights in Barcelona, and prepare a force at Castellon to attack Valencia. Keep a defensive garrison in each owned village.

A.depoimento: Our armies have conquered Toledo, Sevilha, and Salamanca, expanding our kingdom to ten villages. The enemy remains unseen, but we will press our advantage. We are building new troops and preparing the next phase of our campaign.
A.plano: We attacked Toledo, Sevilha, and Salamanca this turn. Next turn we will build up forces in the new villages and prepare to attack Vigo and explore towards Madrid and Cordoba. Keep some troops in reserve to defend the capital.

B.depoimento: Built spearmen in Barcelona, knights in Tarragona and Girona, and an archer in Huesca. Sent three archers from Huesca to seize Pamplona. Sent two spearmen from Barcelona to bolster Tarragona's garrison.
B.plano: Capture Pamplona with archers from Huesca this turn. Reinforce Tarragona and Girona with spearmen from Barcelona. Continue building knights in Tarragona and Girona for future offensives. Hold defensive garrisons; do not attack Valencia yet due to insufficient force.

A.depoimento: Glory to the crown! Your Majesty's armies have triumphed in Madrid and Teruel, securing two vital neutral villages. The clever use of mixed troops to force the spearman counter was a masterstroke. We now hold 12 villages and are on our way to securing the 18 needed for victory!
A.plano: We successfully attacked Madrid and Teruel this turn using the spearman counter tie-break rule. Next turn, we will focus on consolidating our new villages and building up Porto's garrison to prepare for the attack on Vigo and Cordoba. We must continue building archers and knights to counter the enemy's forces.

A.depoimento: Our forces attacked Vigo, Cordoba, and Burgos, while sending a detachment to Valencia. We are expanding rapidly to reach 18 villages and secure our borders.
A.plano: Conquered Vigo, Cordoba, Burgos; sent Toledo to Valencia. Next turn: reinforce new villages, attack Zaragoza, explore unexplored. Keep building troops.

B.depoimento: Recruited infantry across all villages and sent strong reinforcements to the front lines at Castellon and Zaragoza to strengthen our border defenses.
B.plano: Build spearmen for defense and reinforce border villages. Next turn, accumulate more forces at Castellon and Zaragoza to prepare an attack on neutral Valencia or enemy Teruel.

B.depoimento: This turn I raised two spearmen at Castellon and a knight at Zaragoza. I sent Pamplona's garrison to take Burgos and dispatched a mixed force from Zaragoza to probe Teruel.
B.plano: Next turn, build archers at Castellon to prepare an attack on Teruel. Keep Zaragoza defended with remaining spearmen. Hold Burgos if captured and reinforce it. Avoid sending forces to Valencia until we know enemy strength.

A.depoimento: This turn, I have ordered a bold double strike to expand my domain. From Madrid, I am sending spearmen and archers to conquer the lightly defended Burgos, while from Cordoba, a force of archers and a knight marches on the neutral village of Murcia. To secure my flanks, I am rushing reinforcements from Salamanca to Madrid and from Teruel to Valencia, fortifying my borders against the enemy's massive armies in Zaragoza and Castellon. My factories are working overtime, building knights and archers across the realm to fuel this campaign. I will not let the enemy's heavy fortifications stop me from
A.plano: I am focusing on expanding my territory to reach the 18-village threshold for victory. This turn, I am launching a dual attack to conquer the weak enemy village of Burgos from Madrid and the neutral village of Murcia from Cordoba. Simultaneously, I am reinforcing my eastern border by sending troops from Teruel to Valencia and from Salamanca to Madrid to defend against potential enemy counter-attacks from the heavily fortified Zaragoza and Castellon. I am also building troops across my interior villages to maintain a steady flow of reinforcements.

A.depoimento: I have ordered the attack on Pamplona, the last weak enemy village. With my troops from Burgos, I expect to conquer it easily and finally reach the 18 villages needed for victory. I am also reinforcing Burgos and building more knights to secure my borders.
A.plano: I am attacking the empty enemy village of [19] Pamplona from [14] Burgos to conquer it and reach the 18-village threshold for victory. I am sending all available troops from [14] Burgos and reinforcing it from [12] Madrid. I am building knights and archers across my villages to grow my army for the next turns.

B.depoimento: Sent Castellon's army to Valencia and Zaragoza's army to Teruel, reinforced Pamplona with Huesca's spearmen, and held strong garrisons at both border cities. Started knight production at Zaragoza for future strength.
B.plano: Capture Valencia and Teruel next turn while securing Pamplona for future Burgos attack. Keep garrisons at Castellon and Zaragoza to defend against enemy counterattacks. Build knights at Zaragoza to replace losses.

Build archers and knights across all villages to grow the army. Next turn, launch an attack on the empty enemy village [20] Huesca from [19] Pamplona to reach the 18-village threshold for victory.

B.depoimento: Sent Valencia archers and a spear to seize Teruel. Zaragoza troops march on Pamplona. Valencia spears head to strengthen Zaragoza defenses. Started rebuilding a spear and an archer at Zaragoza.
B.plano: Capture Teruel with Valencia archers and spear. Send a mixed force from Zaragoza to take Pamplona. Reinforce Valencia->Zaragoza with spears to bolster defenses after the Pamplona push. Build a spear and an archer at Zaragoza to replace losses. Avoid overextending; keep garrisons at Castellon and Valencia.

A.depoimento: I am launching a decisive offensive to capture the undefended enemy village of Huesca from Pamplona, which will bring my total to 18 villages and put me on the path to victory. At the same time, I am reinforcing Pamplona from Burgos to ensure the enemy's marching army does not retake it, and I am shoring up the defenses of Madrid, Murcia, and Teruel to guard our borders. My army is growing rapidly as I build archers and knights in every village.
A.plano: Capture the empty enemy village [20] Huesca from [19] Pamplona to reach the 18-village threshold for victory. Reinforce [19] Pamplona from [14] Burgos to defend against the enemy army marching toward it. Reinforce border villages [12] Madrid, [15] Murcia, and [13] Teruel from nearby interior villages to prepare for potential enemy attacks. Build archers and knights across all villages to grow the army.

A.depoimento: King A mobilizes the entire realm! All interior troops are marched to the borders to reinforce our hold on the 18 villages. Massive production of knights and archers is ordered across the kingdom, with Huesca producing 6 knights to lead the defense. We will not let the enemy take a single village!
A.plano: We must hold our 18 villages for a second consecutive turn to secure victory. To do this, we are reinforcing all border villages (Madrid, Teruel, Murcia, Pamplona, Huesca) with troops from the interior. We are also building new troops in every village, focusing on knights in resource-rich Huesca and archers/knights elsewhere to maintain our army's strength.

B.depoimento: I sent Valencia's five knights to seize Murcia, trained two archers in Zaragoza, and recruited five spearmen in Barcelona.
B.plano: Next turn, secure Murcia if conquered, continue building spearmen in Barcelona and archers in Zaragoza, and prepare a second knight push from Valencia toward Teruel. Avoid Huesca due to archer counter.

A.depoimento: This turn, we consolidated our defenses by sending reinforcements to our border villages, especially the vulnerable Huesca. Our interior villages produced a steady stream of new troops to maintain our strength. We are on the verge of victory and must hold our ground one more turn to secure the win.
A.plano: We are reinforcing all border villages to hold 18 for victory. Huesca is the weakest, so we sent troops from Pamplona. Madrid, Teruel, and Murcia also received reinforcements. We built new troops everywhere, focusing on knights and archers. Next turn, check if any borders were attacked and adjust defenses. Consider attacking Valencia if we have enough troops to spare without weakening Teruel.
